gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own Apex 300 + 2 × 500W bundle ($3,299) costs $102 more than putting the Apex 300 ($1,499) and the 2-pack of 500 W panels ($1,698) in the same BLUETTI cart, or that each 500 W panel (49.1 V Voc) needs its own Apex 300 solar port, because two panels in series reach 98.2 V and the port limit is 60 V.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited no page. I checked the results it got: the Anker F3800/F3800 Plus product and bundle pages, the Anker F3800 Plus technical brief PDFs, the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus manual and the Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus pages. None covers BLUETTI or OSCAL. None compares a bundle SKU with the same items bought separately. None says how to wire the panels into a 240 V unit's solar ports so they stay under the voltage limit. ChatGPT's answer said only that 'Solar panels may be sold separately'. The bundle-price trap and the one-panel-per-port rule are new. I gave 2, not 3: the wiring rule shapes how the set is connected but does not change which products are picked.
kit_items: 240 V power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W). StorageReview says one unit outputs 120/240 V through its NEMA 14-50R in 240 V mode, so no second unit or hub is needed for 240 V AC. BLUETTI is an approved program and Dealectric already lists this unit as bluetti-apex-300.

Solar panels: 2 × BLUETTI SORA 500 (500 W, MC4). Voc is 49.1 V, under the Apex 300's 60 V port limit, and Isc is 13.31 A, under the 20 A port limit, so each panel goes on its own port. Dealectric lists this panel as bluetti-sora-500-solar-panel.
Alternative 240 V kit in one cart: OSCAL PowerMax 6000 (3,600 Wh, 6,000 W, 120/240 V) + PM400 SE 400 W panel. OSCAL's own kit SKU is $59.99 cheaper than the two items bought separately.

carts.bundle_sku: Apex 300 + 2 × 500W, https://www.bluettipower.com/products/apex-300-2-500w, $3,299.00. That is $102 more than buying the items separately ($1,499 + $1,698 = $3,197), so use the separate items. Apex 300 + 500W, https://www.bluettipower.com/products/apex-300-500w, $2,499.00, is $151 more than $1,499 + $849 = $2,348. Gift: the Apex 300 page shows a 'Free Kid's T-shirt' on most configurations, plus Black Friday Early Access (Nov 5–18) spend-threshold savings and 2X BLUETTI Bucks.

OSCAL Solar Generator Kit 6000W (PowerMax 6000 + PM400 SE), https://store.oscal.hk/products/oscal-solar-generator-kit-6000wpowermax-6000-pm-400se-solar-panel, $1,969.98. That is $59.99 less than buying the items separately ($1,659.99 + $369.98 = $2,029.97), so use the kit SKU. No free gift seen.

findings.note: StorageReview's Kevin OBrien: 'In 240V mode the 14-50R on the side panel carries both lines plus neutral and ground'. In 240 V mode the four front 20 A outlets stay at 120 V. Every DC output needs the $299 Hub D1. The AC outlets do not.

findings.label: Built-in solar input
findings.note: Spec table in the StorageReview review. The BLUETTI product page instead advertises 'up to 4,000W solar input * Requires a SolarX 4K', which is the external charger path.

findings.label: Panel electrical specs
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V; Vmp 40.92 V; Imp 12.22 A; Isc 13.31 A; MC4; 12.9 kg
findings.source_title: Bluetti SORA 500 Foldable Solar Panel (500W), EcoWizard
findings.note: Retailer spec table; BLUETTI's US and EU pages did not load the specs. Arithmetic: 2 in series = 98.2 V Voc, over the Apex 300's 60 V port limit, so use one panel per port. Isc 13.31 A is under the 20 A per-port limit, so each port takes one panel safely and the pair gives 1,000 W of the 2,400 W built-in input.
